messages:
carlos: Quick sync thread: need a concise routing-precedence + eviction playbook for the roadmap doc. Focus: precedence rules across region/tenant/model, soft-eviction behavior, and customer rollback windows.
anya: yes please. customers keep asking how policy conflicts are resolved when region rules and tenant tags disagree.
tim: proposal: precedence order = explicit tenant binding > region-binding > model-profile > default. explicit bindings always win unless explicitly marked as conditional.
carlos: makes sense. we should also define 'eviction' vs 'soft-eviction'. soft-eviction = redirect to fallback pool with telemetry only; eviction = move to lower-priority pool and throttle.
sre-bot: runbook note: soft-eviction should trigger synthetic probe checks and a 10-minute observation window before any throttles. add an auto-unwind if metrics recover.
anya: contract note: provide customers a 4-week migration window during which they can opt-out of enforced slices w/o penalty. sales-bot: flagged.
tim: sample policy fragment (draft):
```yaml
policy_precedence:
  - tenant_binding    # highest
  - region_binding
  - model_profile
  - global_default    # lowest

eviction_policy:
  soft_eviction:
    action: redirect
    target: shared-fallback
    observe_minutes: 10
    metrics_thresholds:
      latency_p99_ms: 40
      error_rate_pct: 0.2
  hard_eviction:
    action: throttle
    throttle_pct: 50
    min_duration_minutes: 30
```
carlos: good. add a quality gate: canonical-eval failure > 7% should count as a hard stop for any rollout.
anya: rollout path for new precedence rules: deploy in observe-only for 1 week, then opt-in customers can try soft routing for 2 weeks, then pilot top 3 tenants for hard enforcement.
sre-bot: add chaos test: simulate region pair outage and confirm fallback policy respects precedence and does not route to blocked region.
sales-bot: ask: can we offer a temporary "priority bridge" for enterprise customers where tenant_binding maps to a reserved tag for 6-12 weeks? pricing TBD.
tim: operational owners: eng-platform owns policy runtime; eng-sre owns probes and rollbacks; product owns migration window + customer comms.
carlos: i'll fold this into the roadmap RFC under a new section "Routing precedence & eviction playbook" and ping legal/sales for the migration window language. please react with :thumbsup: if no objections.
metadata_qa: routing precedence, soft-eviction, eviction policy DSL, rollout path, migration window
